what_happened_next.text:
Microsoft gained the most among these choices, about 148%; Apple gained about 111% and Bank of America about 106%. The U.S. share basket almost doubled, while cash barely grew. The gloomy headlines at the start did not prevent gains, but the ending chart hides many difficult decisions along the way.

Apple reported record September-quarter sales and $8.5 billion in profit in 2014, alongside its biggest iPhone launch to date. Bank of America agreed to a $16.65 billion mortgage-related settlement in 2014, which it said would cut third-quarter pre-tax earnings by $5.3 billion. By 2016, Microsoft reported sharp growth in its Azure cloud service and Office 365. The three examples show different business pressures and opportunities; none alone explains a five-year share result.

A famous investor’s Bank of America deal at the starting date was different from the ordinary shares in this game. Scientists reported a particle consistent with the Higgs boson in 2012, and New Horizons flew past Pluto in 2015. UK voters chose to leave the European Union in 2016, starting a long political process. The same period contained discoveries and decisions beyond company earnings. Looking at the deal and the business matters more than relying on a familiar name.

reflection.what_people_were_focused_on: People worried about government debt and unrest. Apple changed leaders, and a large investor made a special deal with Bank of America.
reflection.what_actually_mattered: The type of investment mattered. Ordinary bank shares did not offer the same terms as Berkshire’s special deal, even though both involved the same bank.
reflection.what_faded_away: The debt downgrade was real, but it did not supply a five-year price forecast. A frightening headline and a falling investment are not the same thing.
reflection.what_nobody_knew: The size of the recovery was unknown. Someone buying then still had to decide how much risk they could handle.

hot:2011-08:apple.text: In October 2014, Apple reported $42.1 billion in sales, a record for its September quarter, and $8.5 billion in net profit. The iPhone 6 and 6 Plus had just become its biggest phone launch yet. Strong iPhone, Mac and App Store sales were helping the business grow.

hot:2011-08:bank-of-america.text: In August 2014, Bank of America agreed to a $16.65 billion settlement over mortgage-related claims. The bank said the deal would reduce third-quarter pre-tax earnings by $5.3 billion. That large cost showed how old loans and legal disputes could still affect a bank years after the housing crisis.

hot:2011-08:microsoft.text: For the quarter ending in June 2016, Microsoft’s Azure cloud revenue grew 102% from a year earlier, and Office 365 business revenue rose 54%. Customers were paying to use software and computing over the internet. These services gave Microsoft growing businesses beyond traditional Windows sales.
